sources: Idempotent consumer pattern under at-least-once delivery (microservices.io): https://microservices.io/patterns/communication-style/idempotent-consumer.html
Timeouts, retries and backoff with jitter (AWS Builders' Library): https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/timeouts-retries-and-backoff-with-jitter/

defects.description: accept_order commits the order row (with conn: block, lines 52-61) and only afterwards calls _publish_order_paid(broker, order) as a separate broker call. Input: a valid Order; the commit succeeds; broker.publish raises ConnectionError on all 3 attempts. Outcome: the order stays persisted with status NEW, accept_order raises ConnectionError, no outbox row exists in the same transaction, and no order_paid event ever reaches the loyalty consumer, violating R1 and R2. The publish is not part of the transaction and no outbox row is written, so a later outbox sweep cannot recover it.

_on_paid reads the balance with get_customer_balance and writes balance + points without any processed message_id check. Input: the same order_paid message with amount '100.00' for customer C is delivered twice (at-least-once redelivery). First call: balance 0 is read, 10 is written. Second call: balance 10 is read, 20 is written. Expected final balance 10 (R3); actual 20.

defects.class: retry amplification without jitter or deadline
defects.description: The caller loop in _publish_order_paid makes PUBLISH_ATTEMPTS=3 outer attempts, each calling publish_with_retry, which itself makes 3 inner attempts (code/outbox_publisher.py:44). Both layers use fixed sleeps (PUBLISH_RETRY_SLEEP=1.0 at outbox_publisher.py:50 and 2.0 at intake.py:78), with no jitter and no overall deadline. Input: a broker outage where every publish raises ConnectionError. Outcome: 9 publish attempts for one message, about 12 s of synchronised fixed sleeps (3 x 2 s outer plus 3 x 2 x 1 s inner), and every worker retries in lockstep. This violates R4.

decoys.why_not_a_defect: The sleep uses exponential backoff with random jitter, and the deadline check at line 62 uses 2 * delay, which is the maximum sleep length. The sleep therefore cannot run past the deadline, so the overall deadline is respected.
A module-level tuple of exception classes used only in except clauses is correct and needs no change. The names ConnectionError and TimeoutError are the intended retryable errors.

The broad except logs the failure with exc_info=True and re-raises with a bare raise at line 65, so the failure is not swallowed or acknowledged silently. The consumer's caller still sees the exception.

fetch_order_status is unchanged by the diff. Its broad except Exception at line 88 returns UNKNOWN for every database error, so an outage is indistinguishable from an unknown order. This is a real flaw on an unchanged line; a diff-mode reviewer must not report it.

accepted_extras.note: balance is read outside the transaction, so concurrent consumers lose an update
